claims.content: The goal of the use case is for the customer to complete payment for won auction items using their chosen method (PayPal or Amazon Payments) within the required timeframe.

scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer completes checkout and pays for won auction items using their chosen payment method within the required timeframe.

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has won auction items and has unpaid winnings to pay for.
The Customer has a registered account with established billing/shipping addresses and payment methods, and the account's default method of payment is either PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The Customer's account is not in Review Status and is not locked due to prior non-payment exceeding policy thresholds.

covered_aspect_ids: account not locked or in Review Status

claims.content: The Customer arrives at the 'Returning Winners Payments Page' after winning auction items.
The system displays the 'PayPal / Amazon Pmts Page for Returning Winners' to the Customer.
The Customer selects the items to pay for from the list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking either the PayPal logo button or the Amazon Payments logo button.
The system launches the checkout process for the selected payment provider.
The Customer completes the selected PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout process within the required timeframe.
Upon completion, the system returns the Customer to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a link to the homepage.
Diverges from Step 4 when the Customer chooses the 'Checkout Later' option: payment is deferred, allowing the Customer to return and pay anytime within 7 days (168 hours) after winning the auction.
Diverges from Step 5 when PayPal is selected: the Customer is immediately taken to the PayPal checkout process on a PayPal-hosted page.
Diverges from Step 5 when Amazon Payments is selected: the Amazon Payments checkout widget loads on the page without leaving the site, graying out the background and disabling other links.

missing_aspects: The claim implies this is an alternative flow or recovery path. The evidence describes it as the standard behavior for the main success scenario ('Clicking on the PayPal logo... immediately takes the user'). If this is intended to be an Alternative Flow (e.g., handling a specific condition), that condition needs to be stated. Otherwise, if it is part of the Main Success Scenario, it should not be in the alternative_flow slot.

The claim implies this is an alternative flow. The evidence describes it as the standard behavior for the main success scenario ('Clicking on the Amazon Payments logo... immediately loads...'). If this is intended to be an Alternative Flow, the triggering condition distinguishing it from the main flow must be specified.

claims.content: At main-flow Step 6 (including when payment was deferred via the 'Checkout Later' alternative), if the Customer does not complete payment for the PayPal or Amazon Payments order within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending/winning, the system automatically cancels the order and places the item into 'Hold' status. Exit: order cancelled.

At main-flow Step 6, when the PayPal or Amazon Payments order expires because payment was not received within 168 hours, the system automatically locks the Customer's account and places it into 'Review Status', preventing the Customer from bidding again until a Customer Service representative unlocks it; the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying for the cancelled order. Exit: account locked/Review Status until Customer Service unlock.

At main-flow Step 4, if the Customer has failed to pay for auction winnings more than three times in a twelve-month period (unless less than 10% of total winnings), the Customer becomes subject to an escalation policy that restricts payment methods to credit cards only, so the PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout option is not available. Exit: PayPal/Amazon payment path unavailable due to credit-card-only restriction.

covered_aspect_ids: non-authorized CC transaction prevention via early charge
payment timeout (168h) leads to order cancellation
hold status pending payment for alternative methods
missing_aspects: No documented exit/continuation for a Customer restricted to credit-card-only payment under the escalation policy.
No documented exception handling for a PayPal or Amazon Payments provider failure before the 168-hour timeout.
No documented handling for a PayPal or Amazon Payments provider failure/error before the 168-hour timeout.
No documented continuation or recovery path for a Customer restricted to credit-card-only payment under the escalation policy within this PayPal/Amazon use case.

claims.content: The Customer has completed payment for the selected won auction items using the chosen PayPal or Amazon Payments method within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time.
The order is not cancelled and does not enter a 'hold' status.
The item's Payment Status is updated to 'Paid' in the My Bid History table.
The Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The system sends a confirmation email stating that another email will be sent shortly confirming the order and shipping information.

covered_aspect_ids: order remains active upon successful payment
no hold status applied after timely payment
